ZLA Sector 18 (West Flow).description:
Sector 18 is primarily a KLAX and KONT departure sector that sequences aircraft proceeding outbound heading northeast; it handles KPSP, KTRM and KUDD arrivals. 
 
Sector 18 is the focal point for several conflicts from other sectors. KPSP departures via V386, or direct PMD that are not yet in high altitude, are pointed out to Sector 18 by Sector 19/20. These aircraft are in conflict with departures from KLAX and KONT towards LAS, which are still in Sector 18's airspace. 
 KONT/KPSP arrivals can be in conflict with the departures off KLAX and KONT toward LAS. The most common remedy is to vector the departure, or the arrival, or both to the east.

ZLA Sector 17 (West Flow).description:
Sector 17 works a complete mix of aircraft. Overtake situations are common, particularly when sequencing aircraft proceeding over PMD for the BUR SCT area or KBUR departures routed over DAG. Burbank jet arrivals must be descended head on with eastbound departure traffic. The new RNAV1 SIDs and STARs have waypoints built in that you can use as crossing restrictions. There will be times when a 'descend via' and a 'climb via' clearance will be used concurrently over the PMD area and the aircraft will be procedureally separated. Ontario and Palm Springs jet arrivals from over PMD can be problematic if left to high by Sector 27. 

SCT Empire area airports arrival traffic are in conflict with Sector 18's departure traffic heading northeast. An alternate routing to KPSP is via V386, this routing is also used by aircraft requesting 15,000 or below in order to remain clear of airports in the vicinity of KONT. The MEA on V386 is 11,000 from APLES to PSP.

ZLA Sector 17/18 Combined (West Flow).description: See individual descriptions for Sectors 17 and 18 for traffic variety and conflict points.

ZLA Sector 04 (West Flow).description:
Sector 04 is a small, complex, fast moving sector. It is 60 miles wide at its widest point and includes airspace 14,000-FL230 over SCT Burbank's airspace, and from the surface to FL230 in the vicinty of GMN and LHS. KLAX,KBUR, and KVNY departures over GMN, and KBUR departures over the PMD area climb into Sector 04's airspace after handoff. 

Sector 04 is primarily a Los Angeles Basin departure sector. It sequences prop/turbo-prop arrival traffic into the basin as well as into Bakersfield (BFL) TRACON airspace. Sector 04 sequences aircraft proceeding into Sectors 03, 17 and 27. 

Traffic conflicts are of three types. First, merging traffic in the above general flows. Traffic must be sequenced (e.g. KLAX GMN and KONT GMN) or crossed (e.g. KONT GMN and V459). Second, traffic crossing the general north and southbound flows. KSBA and KNTD arrival and departure traffic, as well as V12 traffic, fall into this category. Third, traffic proceeds in the opposite direction of the general traffic flows (e.g. J5 traffic southbound). Usually, changing the assigned altitude of the climbing aircraft will resolve the conflict. 

Exercise caution with aircraft routed over COREZ, because Sectors 26 and 27 have control for turns to the west (example: automated point outs from Sector 18)
